facts.fact: The World Bank's appraisal document says paper-based records such as birth and death registrations are currently stored locally across the country without centralised backups, and cites surveys suggesting well over 90% of civil records remain in paper format; it gives no date for this, so the document's date of 8 June 2026 is used.

The Digital Eswatini Project (P508948) allots US$5.5 million of its US$11.5 million IDA-credit sub-component 2.1 to 'Digital ID and Civil Registration', to upgrade the existing ID and civil registration systems, according to the World Bank appraisal document of 8 June 2026.

The World Bank appraisal document of 8 June 2026 sets out a costed activity (US$5.5 million, project closing 31 July 2031) to upgrade the existing ID and civil registration systems and to introduce electronic civil registry services recording births, deaths and marriages, under the government's Digital Transformation Strategy 2024-2028 'Government in Your Hand'; the Ministry of ICT is the implementing agency.
facts.system: existing ID and CR systems; electronic civil registry services

facts.fact: The World Bank appraised the US$65 million Digital Eswatini Project on 8 June 2026 with US$5.5 million for digital ID and civil registration; the document states that the Ministry of ICT confirmed the public services to be digitalised, electronic civil registry services among those it names, are not currently active in the country.
